findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `await isTeamAdmin(...) && await isTeamOwner(...)`. A user who is only an admin or only an owner will fail the check, so legitimate team admins/owners get FORBIDDEN. The intent is clearly admin OR owner. Consequence: broken authorization that denies valid organizers and forces fallback to organizer/attendee checks.

findings.title: Duplicate/blacklist email checks are case-sensitive and miss in-request duplicates
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts uniqueGuests filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where only the blacklist is lowercased, not the incoming guest. An existing attendee `Foo@bar.com` can be re-added as `foo@bar.com`, and a blacklisted address bypasses by case. Duplicates within the `guests` array itself are never deduplicated, unlike the frontend schema. Consequence: duplicate Attendee rows, createMany unique-constraint errors, and blacklist bypass.

findings.title: Wrong guest list passed to email sender misclassifies recipients
findings.body: Handler computes `uniqueGuests` after filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered input. sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between AttendeeScheduledEmail for new guests vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail for old guests. Consequence: existing attendees that were submitted again incorrectly receive a full new-booking invite, and filtered-out addresses affect email routing.

findings.title: No booking status/time validation allows adding guests to cancelled or past bookings
findings.body: addGuests.handler.ts loads the booking by id and only checks existence and caller identity, never checking `status` (CANCELLED/REJECTED) or that start/endTime is in the future. The UI in BookingListItem.tsx also exposes AddGuests via editBookingActions for past confirmed bookings. Consequence: guests can be added to finished or cancelled events, causing confusing calendar updates and emails with stale ICS.

findings.title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of organizer's
findings.body: Handler builds EventManager with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` where ctx.user can be any attendee who passed the isAttendee check, not the booking owner. Updating calendar attendees requires the organizer's calendar credentials. Consequence: when an attendee adds guests the calendar API call fails or updates the wrong calendar, leaving DB, calendar, and emails out of sync.

findings.title: Self-import from @calcom/ui creates circular dependency
findings.body: MultiEmail.tsx lives inside packages/ui but does `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui"`, i.e. importing the package index from within itself. Other form components import directly from relative component paths. Consequence: circular module resolution, larger bundles, and risk of undefined imports at runtime.

findings.title: Unstable React key causes input value mixing
findings.body: In MultiEmail.tsx the email rows are rendered as `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>`. When a middle email is removed via splice, React reuses DOM nodes by index so typed values shift to the wrong row. Consequence: deleting an email can move user input to a different field and submit wrong addresses.

findings.title: Validation error flag never cleared on success
findings.body: AddGuestsDialog.tsx sets `isInvalidEmail` to true on failed validation but only clears it in the Cancel handler, not in handleAdd success path or onSuccess of the mutation which only resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog. Consequence: reopening the dialog after a prior invalid attempt still shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error.
